elections.dateNote: Riksdag rejected Andersson as PM on 15 Oct; government formation ongoing
elections.stakes: The centre-left bloc won a narrow 176-173 majority, ending the right-wing Tido arrangement backed by the Sweden Democrats, but divisions between the Left and Centre parties have stalled government formation.

elections.dateNote: Voting held 18-20 Sep 2026
elections.stakes: United Russia extended its supermajority in a wartime vote held without genuine opposition, consolidating Kremlin control of the legislature; Western governments do not regard the vote as free or fair.

elections.dateNote: King appointed PAM's Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri head of government on 29 Sep 2026; turnout 38%
elections.stakes: PAM overtook outgoing premier Aziz Akhannouch's RNI in a fragmented vote with record-low turnout, while the Islamist PJD staged a comeback; El Mansouri became Morocco's first female head of government.
PM Andris Kulbergs's centre-right United List won a record victory, keeping a firmly pro-Ukraine government in a NATO frontline state, while Russia-friendly populist parties gained in the east.

elections.dateNote: Presidency: Becirovic (Bosniak), Cvijanovic (Serb), Filipovic (Croat)
elections.stakes: Record-low turnout returned largely familiar ethnic parties; Dodik's SNSD kept control in Republika Srpska, sustaining secessionist pressure that tests the Dayton settlement and the EU path.
elections.winner: Presidency: Denis Becirovic, Zeljka Cvijanovic, Darijana Filipovic

elections.dateNote: No majority: runoff on 25 Oct between Flavio Bolsonaro and Lula
elections.seats: President, 513 Chamber of Deputies seats, 54 of 81 Senate seats
elections.stakes: Latin America's largest economy split almost evenly between Lula's left and the Bolsonaro right, with implications for Amazon policy, BRICS and relations with Washington.

elections.dateNote: First round 25 Oct: Yotova 34.76%, Gyurov 31.95% (CEC), turnout 22.98%. Runoff 1 Nov 2026.
elections.stakes: Incumbent Iliana Yotova, backed by PM Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria, faces pro-Western challenger Andrey Gyurov in a 1 November runoff. The race is seen as a test of Radev's government and of Bulgaria's stance on Russia and Ukraine.

elections.dateNote: Single-round vote; no runoff. Vote shares from RIK preliminary count of 26 Oct; seats updated 28 Oct after votes abroad were counted; official final RIK results
elections.stakes: After nearly two years of student-led protests, the Student List won an outright majority, ending the Serbian Progressive Party's 14 years in power. The outcome will shape Serbia's balance between the EU and Russia.

elections.dateNote: Runoff held 25 Oct; first round 4 Oct, Flavio Bolsonaro led Lula by over 2.2 million votes
elections.stakes: The runoff decided whether Lula would win a fourth term or the Bolsonaro family would return to power, a choice with implications for Brazil's climate, trade and foreign-policy direction.

elections.dateNote: Vote held 27 Oct 2026; final count published 30 Oct; no bloc reached 61 seats; certification due 4 Nov
elections.stakes: First general election since the 7 October 2023 attack and the Gaza war; decides whether Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing and religious coalition keeps power, shaping policy on Gaza, Iran and the West Bank.

elections.dateNote: Tuesday; early voting in many states beforehand
elections.stakes: Control of Congress for the second half of Donald Trump's term, deciding how much of his agenda on tariffs, immigration and spending can pass.

elections.dateNote: Advance voting from 26 Oct; official results 27 Nov
elections.stakes: Tests Christopher Luxon's National-ACT-NZ First coalition against a Labour-Green bloc. Recent polls show neither bloc clearly ahead, leaving the Opportunity Party as a possible kingmaker.

elections.dateNote: Called by Pedro Sanchez on 5 Oct 2026; date confirmed for 29 Nov
elections.stakes: Sanchez called an early vote after Congress rejected his housing decrees. Polls point to a PP-led government that would need Vox, bringing the far right into government in a major EU economy.

elections.dateNote: Four federal questions on one ballot
elections.stakes: Voters decide on a 0.4-point VAT rise to help fund the 13th pension, looser war-materiel export rules for partner states in conflict, a fireworks restriction and joint taxation of married couples.

elections.dateNote: Must be held by 27 Dec 2026; date not yet set
elections.stakes: Vucic's resignation forces an early presidential vote, held separately from the parliamentary election on 25 October. It will show whether the ruling SNS can keep the presidency as he moves to the premiership.

elections.dateNote: Earliest possible date; not yet confirmed, pending validation of signatures
elections.stakes: Voters would decide whether to lift the ban on building new nuclear power plants, which parliament approved in June 2026. Supporters cite winter electricity security and climate goals; opponents cite cost, radioactive waste and the growth of renewables.

elections.dateNote: Advance voting 1–6 Mar 2027
elections.stakes: Isamaa leads the latest polling trend ahead of the Centre Party, while Prime Minister Kristen Michal's Reform Party has fallen to about 13 percent. The result could bring a change of government in this NATO frontline state bordering Russia.

elections.dateNote: Runoff 2 May 2027
elections.stakes: With Emmanuel Macron barred from a third term, the far-right National Rally leads every poll, raising the prospect of a eurosceptic president with control of a nuclear power's foreign policy.
The opposition Social Democrats lead over PM Petteri Orpo's coalition, which includes the nationalist Finns Party; NATO's newest frontline member with Russia faces a likely change of government.

elections.dateNote: PM says spring 2027; legal deadline 25 Jul 2027
elections.stakes: Kyriakos Mitsotakis seeks a third term but New Democracy polls near 30%, short of a majority, while Alexis Tsipras's new left party has become the main challenger.

elections.dateNote: Due before 30 Jun 2027; date not set
elections.stakes: A leading EU accession candidate votes with PM Milojko Spajic's Europe Now! trailing the former ruling DPS and the pro-Serbian For the Future of Montenegro in polls.

elections.dateNote: Planned for June 2027; date not yet set by Federal Council
elections.stakes: Voters decide whether to approve the Bilaterals III package of updated and new EU agreements, including rules on free movement of people and dispute settlement. Approval would shape Switzerland's relationship with the EU for the next decade.

elections.dateNote: Usually held in the first half of June; date not set
elections.stakes: Incumbent Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh is term-limited; the race between the ruling MPP and the Democratic Party sets the tone for Mongolia's democracy sandwiched between Russia and China.
First midterm test for President Claudia Sheinbaum; Morena and allies seek to keep their supermajority in the Chamber of Deputies.

elections.dateNote: Date set by parliament speaker; term expires autumn 2027
elections.stakes: Liberal Progressive Slovakia narrowly leads Robert Fico's Smer, whose government has softened support for Ukraine and clashed with Brussels over rule of law; the result shapes Slovakia's alignment with Hungary.

elections.dateNote: Due by 11 Nov 2027; President sets date (Oct-Nov Sundays/holidays)
elections.stakes: Donald Tusk's pro-EU coalition leads but may lack a majority, while a combined right including two far-right Confederations could return; key for Ukraine support and EU rule-of-law politics.

elections.dateNote: Parliament's term ends; must be held by 22 Dec 2027; government says October 2027
elections.stakes: Giorgia Meloni seeks re-election after a full term; polls show her Brothers of Italy leading but a combined centre-left ahead of the centre-right coalition.

elections.dateNote: Due by Oct-Nov 2027; date not set; runoff if needed
elections.stakes: Incumbent liberal independent Natasa Pirc Musar is eligible for a second term but undeclared; former president Borut Pahor has not ruled out a return.

elections.seats: 200 National Council + 46 Council of States seats
elections.stakes: The national-conservative SVP is polling near 30%; the election comes as Switzerland debates ratifying a new treaty package with the EU, which the SVP opposes.

elections.dateNote: Runoff likely 21 Nov 2027 if needed
elections.stakes: Javier Milei seeks re-election as a referendum on his libertarian shock therapy, against a Peronist opposition seeking a comeback.

elections.dateNote: January 2028; exact day not confirmed
elections.seats: President and vice president; 113 Legislative Yuan seats
elections.stakes: Decides whether the ruling DPP keeps the presidency for a second term or power passes to the opposition, with major implications for cross-strait policy. Control of the legislature is also at stake.
